conflicts.description: frontend api.user.list calls GET /users but the graph defines no such endpoint
conflicts.impact: the frontend feature using this call will receive 404/405 from the backend
conflicts.recommended_resolution: add the operation + endpoint to the Graph (preferred) or change the frontend call; the backend does not invent endpoints

conflicts.description: entity.task.status: frontend uses ['TODO', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'COMPLETED'] but graph uses ['todo', 'in_progress', 'completed'] (same values, different case)
conflicts.impact: every write of this enum from the frontend is rejected (422); every read is displayed with the wrong case
conflicts.recommended_resolution: normalise enum casing in one place (the graph is the source of truth)

conflicts.description: frontend entity.project.created_at is not in the graph response schema (graph fields: ['description', 'due_date', 'id', 'name', 'owner_id', 'status'])
conflicts.impact: the UI will show an empty/undefined 'created_at'
conflicts.recommended_resolution: rename in the frontend or add 'created_at' to the graph entity/response

conflicts.description: frontend entity.task.created_at is not in the graph response schema (graph fields: ['assignee_id', 'description', 'due_date', 'id', 'project_id', 'status', 'title'])
conflicts.impact: the UI will show an empty/undefined 'created_at'
conflicts.recommended_resolution: rename in the frontend or add 'created_at' to the graph entity/response

conflicts.description: frontend entity.user.name is not in the graph response schema (graph fields: ['created_at', 'email', 'full_name', 'id', 'role'])
conflicts.impact: the UI will show an empty/undefined 'name'
conflicts.recommended_resolution: rename in the frontend or add 'name' to the graph entity/response

conflicts.description: api.task.create sends 'assignee_id' but graph schema schema.task.create does not define it
conflicts.impact: the backend rejects unknown fields (mass-assignment protection): requests carrying 'assignee_id' get 422
conflicts.recommended_resolution: add 'assignee_id' to the graph's request schema/operation input, or stop sending it

conflicts.description: api.task.create sends 'description' but graph schema schema.task.create does not define it
conflicts.impact: the backend rejects unknown fields (mass-assignment protection): requests carrying 'description' get 422
conflicts.recommended_resolution: add 'description' to the graph's request schema/operation input, or stop sending it

conflicts.description: api.task.create sends 'due_date' but graph schema schema.task.create does not define it
conflicts.impact: the backend rejects unknown fields (mass-assignment protection): requests carrying 'due_date' get 422
conflicts.recommended_resolution: add 'due_date' to the graph's request schema/operation input, or stop sending it

conflicts.description: api.task.list sends query parameter 'project_id' that the graph does not define for api.task.list
conflicts.impact: the filter is ignored/rejected by the backend
conflicts.recommended_resolution: define the filter in the graph operation

conflicts.description: 'description' is required by graph schema schema.project.create but optional in the frontend (api.project.create)
conflicts.impact: the frontend may omit it and receive 422
conflicts.recommended_resolution: make 'description' optional in the graph or required in the frontend form

conflicts.description: frontend login expects {token, user} but api.user.login responds with schema.user which has no token
conflicts.impact: without a token the frontend cannot authenticate any later request
conflicts.recommended_resolution: add a session response schema (token + user) to api.json
conflicts.resolution_applied: login returns the session envelope {token, token_type, expires_in, user} and ALSO the user fields at top level, so both the graph schema and the frontend Session type are satisfied

conflicts.description: frontend allows completed -> in_progress for entity.task but state_machine.task does not
conflicts.impact: the UI offers a transition the backend refuses with 409 (the backend never allows undeclared transitions)
conflicts.recommended_resolution: add the transition to the graph state machine or remove it from the frontend

conflicts.description: no operation creates entity.user: users can log in but cannot be created through the API
conflicts.impact: the product cannot onboard its first user via the API
conflicts.recommended_resolution: add a create-user (or self-registration) operation to the graph
conflicts.resolution_applied: generated backend ships `python -m backend_app.manage create-user` for provisioning

conflicts.description: validation.task.completed_needs_assignee depends on entity.task.assignee_id but no operation in the graph can set it
conflicts.impact: the rule can never be satisfied/exercised through the API (e.g. tasks can never get an assignee)
conflicts.recommended_resolution: add 'assignee_id' to an operation's input (e.g. on create/update or a dedicated assign operation)

conflicts.description: the backend error contract is {error:{code,message,details}} while the frontend client reads top-level {message, errors}
conflicts.impact: without a shim the frontend would show only generic messages and no field errors
conflicts.recommended_resolution: keep one canonical shape in the Frontend client
conflicts.resolution_applied: every error body carries BOTH: {error:{code,message,details}, message, errors, request_id}

conflicts.description: operation.project.progress is an aggregate but its response schema is the plain entity list (schema.project)
conflicts.impact: aggregate numbers have no contractual place in the response
conflicts.recommended_resolution: add a dedicated aggregate response schema in api.json

conflicts.description: password reset operations exist but the graph defines no entity for reset tokens or sessions
conflicts.recommended_resolution: model reset tokens / sessions as an entity if persistence or revocation across instances is required
conflicts.resolution_applied: stateless signed reset tokens bound to the current password hash; in-process token revocation list
